The relation is payment-invariant: on any fixture whose live population is even with differing middles, the persisted ceiling is an integer equal to the pre-move base plus the floored product, and the unfloored form would persist the fractional value on the identical fixture. Failure: any derivation site persisting `X.5`. The instrument is the shipped suite: the `C-ROOT-WINDOW floored derivation` test drives both directions on the identical fixture, and the `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY clamp invariant` holds the persisted headroom to the clamp's result.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-WINDOW-UNMOVED:
On a successful `--retire` move, a genre with zero moved elements keeps its persisted ceiling and has its base re-derived from its shipped metric read back, so its window survives moves in unrelated genres; a genre with moved elements keeps the shipped moving-genre arithmetic (persisted ceiling = `min(previous ceiling, pre-move base + floored headroom)`); the index is re-derived when its `<Entry>` layers flip and held otherwise. This criterion is governed by the carried `Clarification` targeting `<INV-ROOT-WINDOW-UNMOVED />`, resolved by the maintainer as recommended, and states the resolution's semantics. After any successful move, every live root satisfies `base + headroom = ceiling` with `base` equal to its shipped metric read back, and a genre whose bytes the move did not change keeps its persisted ceiling. The instrument is the shipped suite: the `C-ROOT-WINDOW unmoved window` test (whose title names the shipped clamp — `C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW`'s min-not-decorative behaviour — as the named baseline it overturns), the `C-ROOT-WINDOW unmoved window across two consecutive moves` test, and the moving-genre `T-001 window` tests that pass unchanged. Failure: an unmoved genre's window shrinking across a move in another genre, or a moved genre failing the shipped relations.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-INDENT-NORMALISED:
The move's writer normalises the inter-element whitespace of every file it writes (a genre with removals, a retired sibling with appends, the index when its layers flip), and treats top-level comments as units — the semantic its predecessor stated for the first time: a top-level comment's bytes pass through in place, the gaps around units are rewritten to the canonical house shape (`<newline><two spaces>` before a unit, `<newline>` before the root close tag, the tail preserved), every surviving element's own bytes are byte-identical to their pre-pass bytes, and any other non-whitespace content in an inter-element gap refuses the pass loudly before any write. The pass touches no file the move did not write, so a genre with zero moved elements keeps its bytes (its pre-existing drift stays until its own move normalises it — measured, and stated in the `Goal`). The instrument is the shipped suite: the `C-ROOT-WINDOW normalising pass` test (element bytes byte-identical, canonical gaps, a mutated element's own bytes reddening the walk) and the `rulings window clamped` test, whose fixture's 1800 load-bearing top-level comments pass through a real move. Clarifications.Clarification: Resolved 2026-09-11 by the maintainer, as recommended: a genre the move did not change keeps its persisted ceiling; `base` is re-derived from its shipped metric read back and `headroom` is the remainder. The moving genre keeps the shipped `persistSnapshot` arithmetic. One rule, shared by the move and the mode. `F193`'s window semantics for a genre with zero moved elements. Two candidates were driven on throwaway copies at this commit. **Recommendation — persist the opened window (hold the ceiling, re-derive the base):** a genre the move did not change keeps its persisted ceiling and gets `base` from its shipped metric read back, `headroom` as the remainder; the moving genre keeps the shipped `persistSnapshot` arithmetic. Pros: the shipped all-roots tripwire (`base + headroom = ceiling`, `base` equals its metric — asserted after every successful move by the shipped `T-001 window` test at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:692` and by the production roots invariant) stays true without depending on anyone running the mode, so the move remains self-healing for hand-drift in every genre; the fix is one rule shared with the mode; only the one shipped test that pins the clamp (the `min not decorative` test) needs rewriting, and the moving-genre window test passes unchanged. Cons: the unmoved genre's open-tag splice makes its byte-identity empirical rather than structural (measured byte-identical at any consistent record; a drifted record reddens the criterion and stops the close — the honest outcome), and a hand-raised ceiling in an unmoved genre now survives unrelated moves (it is lowered by its own genre's next move — stated in the Known-boundary `Constraint`). **Runner-up — re-derive only the genre that moved:** pros: the unmoved genre is structurally untouched, so its byte-invariance is structural; cons: it abandons the shipped invariant that every live root satisfies the relations after any successful move — the shipped validator has no base-versus-metric check, so a drifted unmoved genre would survive a legitimate move with the validator green, and the drift would surface only later in the production tripwire; three shipped tests need rewriting instead of one. The runner-up loses because its only advantage (structural byte-invariance for one file) is bought by weakening a shipped invariant the record's enforcement posture relies on, and the same cleanliness is reachable under the recommendation by parse-based relations. Governs `AC-WINDOW-UNMOVED` and, for the byte-invariance reasoning, `AC-RECORD-UNMOVED`.

Resolved 2026-09-11 by the maintainer, as recommended: round down (`Math.floor`) at every derivation site. On an integer median the floor is the identity; on a `.5` median it is the only direction that cannot loosen a budget. `F182`'s rounding direction. **Recommendation — round down (`Math.floor`) at every derivation site:** verified against the shipped clamp (`persistSnapshot`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:950`): the persisted ceiling is `min(persisted ceiling, base + headroom)` and headroom is ceiling minus base, so a larger formula term can only hold or raise the persisted ceiling — equal-or-looser — and only rounding down can never loosen a budget; on an integer median the floor is the identity, so the fix changes nothing today. Pros: budgets tighten or hold, never loosen; the relation survives every later move. Cons: the persisted window can be one line tighter than the unfloored arithmetic would have given on a `.5` median — that is the point. **Runner-up — round half up (`Math.round`):** on a `.5` it rounds away from the tighter budget, which is exactly the direction `D28` forbids loosening in; **half-to-even** rounds down or up by parity, so it can loosen and is refused by the same argument. The runner-ups lose on direction, not on style. Governs `AC-ROUNDING-FLOOR`.

Resolved 2026-09-11 by the maintainer, as recommended: `--rewrite-roots` holds every ceiling byte-for-byte, re-derives `base` from the shipped metric and `headroom` as the remainder, and refuses (exit 1, nothing written) when a genre's count exceeds its persisted ceiling or a ceiling attribute is missing. Together with the resolution above this ratifies the record's invariant: a ceiling is written only by `--retire`, and only downward; every other writer holds it. The mode's ceiling semantics. **Recommendation — hold (pass through):** `--rewrite-roots` never writes a ceiling attribute different from the one it read; it re-derives `base` from the shipped metric and `headroom` as ceiling minus base, and refuses (exit 1, nothing written) when a genre's count exceeds its persisted ceiling or a ceiling attribute is missing. Pros: structurally incapable of raising a ceiling (`D28`), incapable of adopting or recomputing one, and it repairs exactly the hand-drift `F216` records — the post-write registry state (base grown, ceiling held, headroom the remainder) is what every hand-write has produced since the split, driven. Cons: it cannot lower a hand-raised ceiling — the Known-boundary `Constraint` states what that leaves open. **Runner-up — formula with clamp (re-derive the ceiling as `min(persisted, base + floored H)`):** pros: lowers hand-raises back to the formula. Cons: it closes every window a retirement opened whenever the formula's term has fallen below the persisted ceiling — `F193`'s defect reintroduced through the mode, the exact behaviour this bundle exists to stop — and on a normal post-write record, where the formula's term exceeds the held ceiling, the clamp reduces to the hold anyway. The runner-up loses on the record's own design. Governs `AC-MODE-SHIPPED`.
